1.title: The Daily Loop: Stage, Commit, Inspect
1.text: Welcome to Module two: The Daily Loop: Stage, Commit, Inspect. It covers the exam area Part one: Foundations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Stage and commit with git add and git commit. Read git status and its short codes. Compare changes with git diff and git diff --staged. Read history with git log and git show. Remove and rename files with git rm and git mv. Ignore files with.git ignore. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: The loop: status, add, commit
1.text: The loop: status, add, commit. Daily work is a loop: edit files, check with git status, stage with git add, and record with git commit. The figure shows the loop. git status tells you the next command, so run it often.

1.title: The loop: status, add, commit, continued
1.text: The loop: status, add, commit. The figure shows this: The daily loop: edit files in the working tree, stage them with git add, record them with git commit, and inspect with status, diff and log.

1.title: The loop: status, add, commit, continued
1.text: The loop: status, add, commit. git status dash s is the short form. It prints two columns: the first compares the staging area with the last commit, the second compares the working tree with the staging area. ?? New file that Git does not track yet. A in column one. New file, staged. M in column one. Modified and staged. M in column two. Modified, not staged. M M. Staged, then edited again. D. Deleted: staged in column one, not staged in column two. R. Renamed and staged. U U. Unmerged conflict (module four).

1.title: The loop: status, add, commit, continued
1.text: The loop: status, add, commit. git add file. That file. git add. Every new, changed and deleted file here and below. git add dash p. Only the hunks you answer yes to, one at a time. git commit dash a. Edits to tracked files, then commits; new files stay out. git commit dash m message records the staging area. Without dash m, Git opens your editor for the message. Your hashes will differ from the ones in this module.

1.title: Reading changes: diff, log and show
1.text: Reading changes: diff, log and show. Three git diff forms answer three questions. git diff. Working tree against the staging area: unstaged edits. git diff the staged flag. Staging area against the last commit: what you will commit. git diff head. Working tree against the last commit: everything.

1.title: Reading changes: diff, log and show, continued
1.text: Reading changes: diff, log and show. the stat flag gives a summary and the name only flag lists only the file names. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Reading changes: diff, log and show, continued
1.text: Reading changes: diff, log and show. After git add, plain git diff is empty and git diff the staged flag shows the change. git log lists commits, newest first. git show prints one commit with its message and patch. git show head tilde one shows the parent, and git show head cart dot txt prints a file as it was in a commit.

1.title: Reading changes: diff, log and show, continued
1.text: Reading changes: diff, log and show. the oneline flag. One line per commit. the graph flag the decorate flag the all flag. Draw the branches and show their names. dash p. Add the patch of each commit. the stat flag. Add the changed files and counts. dash n three. Only the last three commits. the author flag set to Bob. Only commits by Bob. the since flag set to two weeks ago. Only recent commits. -- cart dot txt. Only commits that touched this path.

1.title: Reading changes: diff, log and show, continued
1.text: Reading changes: diff, log and show. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Tip: Run git diff the staged flag before every commit. It shows exactly what the commit will contain, so surprises stay out of history.

1.title: Remove, rename and ignore
1.text: Remove, rename and ignore. git rm file deletes the file and stages the deletion. git rm the cached flag file stops tracking a file but keeps it in your folder. git mv old new renames a file and stages the rename, and git status dash s shows an R. Moving a file by hand and then running git add gives the same result, because Git detects renames from the content. A dot git ignore file lists patterns for files Git should leave alone. Commit it, so the whole team shares the rules.

1.title: Remove, rename and ignore, continued
1.text: Remove, rename and ignore. dot log. Any file ending in.log, in any folder. build slash. Any folder named build. !keep dot log. Exception: keep tracking this file. slash todo dot txt. Only the todo.txt at the repository root. dot git slash info slash exclude. Personal rules for this clone, not shared. Ignore rules only affect files that are not tracked yet. A file that is already committed stays tracked, and git status keeps showing its changes. An exception also cannot reach into an ignored folder. git check ignore dash v file names the line that ignores a file.

1.text: Remove, rename and ignore. Four new files exist, yet only dot git ignore and keep dot log are listed. Tip: Adding a pattern does not untrack a committed file; run git rm the cached flag file once. Then commit, and the rule applies from then on.

1.title: A good commit and amend
1.text: A good commit and amend. A good commit has one logical change that you can describe in one line. The subject is in the imperative mood, as if giving an order: "Add free shipping rule", not "Added" or "Adds". Keep it to about fifty characters. If the reason is not obvious, add a blank line and a short body that says why.

2.title: A good commit and amend, continued
2.text: A good commit and amend. fix stuff. Fix cart total when a coupon is used. Updated files and added things. Add free shipping rule to cart. One commit with a bug fix and a rename. Two commits, one change each. git commit the amend flag replaces the last commit. Use dash m to fix the message, or git add a forgotten file and run git commit the amend flag the no edit flag. The result is a new commit with a new hash, and the old one is gone from the branch.

2.text: A good commit and amend. The message is the same, but the hash changed, so this is a new commit. The tax file joined the commit. Tip: Amend only commits you have not shared. Others may already have the old hash, and a changed hash causes trouble (module six covers the safe ways to undo).

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. git status dash s prints?? notes dot txt and M cart dot txt. Which statement is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: notes.txt is untracked and cart.txt has unstaged edits. The double question mark marks a file Git does not track, and an M in the second column marks an edit that is not staged.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Ada staged cart.txt and then edited it again. Which command shows only the newer edit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: git diff, which compares the folder with the staging area. Plain git diff compares the working tree with the staging area, so it shows only what is not staged.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Cy committed debug.log by mistake, then added dot log to.git ignore. git status still shows changes to debug.log. What fixes it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git rm the cached flag debug dot log, then commit the removal. Ignore rules do not apply to tracked files, so the file must be untracked first, and the cached flag keeps it in the folder.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Bob sees a typo in the message of his last commit. Nothing has been shared. What is the safest fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: git commit the amend flag dash m with the corrected message. Amend rewrites only the last commit, which is fine while no one else has it.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Ada wants the message and the patch of the commit just before the last one. Which command does it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git show head tilde one, which prints the parent commit and its patch. git show prints one commit with its message and patch, and head tilde one names the parent of the last commit.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Which commit message best follows the guidance for a good commit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Add free shipping for orders above the set threshold. It describes one change in the imperative mood and is about fifty characters, while the others are past tense, vague or mixed.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command shows what is staged for the next commit? Answer: git diff the staged flag. Question two. What does git add dash p let you do? Answer: Stage chosen hunks of a file instead of the whole file. Question three. Which command renames a tracked file and stages the rename? Answer: git mv old new.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command stops tracking a file but keeps it in your folder? Answer: git rm the cached flag. Question five. Which command shows the dot git ignore line that ignores a file? Answer: git check ignore dash v. Question six. How long and in which mood should a commit subject be? Answer: About fifty characters, in the imperative mood.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Loop: Edit, git status, git add, git commit dash m, inspect. Short status:?? untracked; M modified; A added; D deleted; R renamed; two columns. Staging: git add file, git add., git add dash p; git commit dash a skips new files. Diff: git diff unstaged; git diff the staged flag staged; git diff head both. History: git log the oneline flag the graph flag the decorate flag the all flag; dash p, the stat flag, dash n, the author flag, the since flag. Show: git show for one commit; git show head file for an old file. Remove, rename: git rm, git rm the cached flag, git mv. Ignore: dot log, build slash,!keep dot log; tracked files are not ignored; git check ignore dash v. Good commit: One change, imperative subject, about fifty characters; amend only unshared commits.
